domain_label: Knowledge Organization Systems (KOS) — Information Science subdomain
purpose: Provide a session-bounded, subdomain-grain ontology of Knowledge Organization Systems work units (KOS scope/type selection and reuse, warrant analysis, concept and relation modeling, equivalence/synonymy control, precoordination vs postcoordination, facet analysis, notation/URI design, SKOS serialization, subject headings, name authority, gazetteers, terminology management, vocabulary mapping/alignment, governance/versioning, and evaluation) to plan, evaluate, sequence, validate, and lock the design or adoption of controlled vocabularies for finding, retrieving, and synthesizing authoritative knowledge.
assumptions: Parent domain is information_science_and_knowledge_organization; this KB models the Knowledge Organization Systems (KOS) subdomain at subdomain grain.
No observed dataset, benchmark, or expert-judgment input was supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Each node is a single KOS work unit, method, or decision area sized for one heavy reasoning session.
User tasks, domain scope, and warrant sources are parameters the workflow profiles before locking structure.
Both build-new and adopt-existing KOS paths are in scope; SKOS is the default interoperable representation.
exclusions: Full-text and vector/embedding retrieval modeling (covered by other information-retrieval KBs).
Cataloging description rules (RDA/MARC record structure) beyond access-point and authority concerns.
Domain-specific subject content authoring (the actual concepts of any one discipline).
Search-engine ranking, indexing data structures, and query processing internals.
Folksonomy/social-tagging system design except as a contrasted non-controlled alternative.

competency_questions.question: Should we build a new KOS or adopt/reuse an existing one for this domain and tasks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KOS_SCOPE_NEED and KOS_SELECT_REUSE present with a build-vs-reuse output

competency_questions.question: Which KOS type fits the domain scope and user tasks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KOS_SCOPE_NEED and KOS_TYPE_SELECT present with selection rationale

competency_questions.question: What expressivity and interoperability level does the selected type require?
Which terms and structure are justified by literary, user, and structural warrant?
How are concepts distinguished from terms, and how is synonymy controlled?
How are broader/narrower relations modeled with correct generic vs partitive semantics?
When is a related-term (RT) link appropriate instead of a hierarchical link?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASSOC_REL and HIERARCHY_REL present with sequence edge between them

competency_questions.question: Are subjects coordinated at index time or search time, and with what citation order?
How is the KOS decomposed into facets and how is fitness evaluated?
How are notation/identifiers designed for stability and growth?
How is the KOS represented in SKOS and validated for integrity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SKOS_SERIALIZE and KOS_EVALUATION present with dependency edge

competency_questions.question: How are subject headings, name authorities, places, and terms controlled as access points?
How are vocabularies mapped/aligned and how is mapping precision governed?
How is the KOS governed, versioned, and changed without breaking consumers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOVERNANCE_VERSION present with versioning and deprecation

glossary.definition: controlled structure organizing concepts and terms for retrieval and browse
language-independent unit of thought identified independently of the terms naming it
a label (word/phrase) that names a concept
controlled vocabulary with equivalence, hierarchical, and associative relations
hierarchical classification of concepts via broader/narrower relations
formal specification of concepts and relations with logical axioms
Simple Knowledge Organization System, an RDF model for KOS publication
justification (literary, user, or structural) for including a term or structure
combining subjects into a single string at indexing time
combining separate subject terms at search time
a fundamental, mutually exclusive category used to analyze a domain
a mapping between concepts of two or more vocabularies

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established knowledge-organization literature and practice (Joudrey & Taylor 2017; Chan & Salaba 2015; Svenonius 2000); no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Determine the domain scope, user tasks, and warrant that justify building or adopting a KOS and what type is required.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when user tasks, domain boundary, or collection composition shift materially

pros.claim: prevents building the wrong KOS type for the task
pros.example: choosing a thesaurus when a flat taxonomy would serve browse-only needs

cons.claim: scope errors propagate into every downstream modeling and mapping decision
cons.example: under-scoping omits a subdomain that later forces a vocabulary split

failure_modes: scope set by collection not user tasks
acceptance_tests: scope statement names user tasks and warrant types

nodes.definition: Select the KOS structure family (term list, classification scheme, taxonomy, thesaurus, ontology, subject-heading list, terminology, gazetteer, name authority) fitting scope and tasks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when expressivity needs or interoperability targets change

pros.claim: matches structural cost to actual retrieval/browse requirements
pros.example: selecting a thesaurus only when synonym control and RT/BT relations are needed

cons.claim: over-rich types raise authoring and maintenance cost without payoff
cons.example: an ontology built where a taxonomy suffices burdens contributors

failure_modes: type chosen by trend not need
mixing incompatible type semantics in one artifact
acceptance_tests: selected type supports all required user tasks
revisit_triggers: new interoperability target requires richer semantics
authoring cost exceeds value of expressivity

nodes.definition: Decide which terms and structure are justified using literary, user, and structural warrant.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when corpus or query distribution shifts term frequency/coverage

pros.claim: grounds the vocabulary in real usage rather than designer intuition
pros.example: adding a term because query logs show recurring demand

cons.claim: warrant sources can conflict and need an explicit precedence rule
cons.example: literary warrant supports a term users never search for

acceptance_tests: each included term cites a warrant source
revisit_triggers: query logs diverge from corpus vocabulary

nodes.definition: Model concepts as language-independent units of thought distinct from the terms/labels that name them.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when terms split/merge into distinct or unified concepts

pros.claim: separating concept from term enables multilingual labels and synonym control
pros.example: one concept 'automobile' carries preferred label plus synonyms 'car','motorcar'

cons.claim: concept identity decisions are hard to reverse once URIs are minted
cons.example: merging two concepts later orphans references to a retired URI

failure_modes: term treated as concept causing synonym duplication
acceptance_tests: each concept has exactly one preferred label per language
revisit_triggers: two concepts found to be synonymous

nodes.definition: Establish broader/narrower (BT/NT) relations with correct generic, instance, and partitive distinctions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when concepts are added that change a branch's genus-species logic

pros.claim: enables hierarchical browse, query expansion, and inference
pros.example: narrowing 'dogs' under 'mammals' supports broaden/narrow navigation

cons.claim: mixing isA with part-of breaks transitive inference
cons.example: placing 'wheel' as NT of 'car' under an isA reading corrupts subsumption

acceptance_tests: each BT asserts a single relation kind

nodes.definition: Define related-term (RT) associative links between concepts that are neither equivalent nor hierarchical.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when users report missing cross-references between sibling areas

pros.claim: surfaces useful lateral navigation and recall improvements
pros.example: linking 'birds' RT 'ornithology' aids discovery across branches

cons.claim: over-linking RTs dilutes precision and inflates maintenance
cons.example: every loosely related pair linked making RT navigation noisy

failure_modes: RT used where BT/NT is correct
acceptance_tests: RT not duplicating a hierarchical path
revisit_triggers: RT density per concept exceeds threshold

nodes.definition: Control equivalence: choose preferred terms and manage synonyms, lexical variants, and USE/UF references.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new lexical variants or near-synonyms appear in the corpus

pros.claim: collapses variant spellings to one access point improving recall
pros.example: 'colour' and 'color' resolve to one preferred term

cons.claim: forcing near-synonyms into equivalence loses precision distinctions
cons.example: treating 'efficacy' and 'effectiveness' as equivalent erases a real distinction

acceptance_tests: each synonym ring has one preferred term
revisit_triggers: new variant spellings recur in corpus

nodes.definition: Decide where subjects are combined: at indexing time (precoordinated strings) or at search time (postcoordinated terms).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when retrieval system gains/loses postcoordination capability

pros.claim: controls precision/recall tradeoff and false-coordination risk
pros.example: postcoordination avoids enumerating every subject combination as a string

cons.claim: precoordination citation-order errors cause false drops and hits
cons.example: wrong facet order buries a heading users cannot predict

acceptance_tests: citation order rules documented and applied consistently

nodes.definition: Analyze a domain into mutually exclusive facets and fix citation/combination order for faceted KOS.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when concepts cannot be cleanly assigned to existing facets

pros.claim: yields compact, extensible structure avoiding combinatorial enumeration
pros.example: facets for material, process, and product compose flexibly

cons.claim: facet boundaries and citation order are contested and hard to revise
cons.example: reassigning a concept's facet ripples through every combined notation

failure_modes: citation order changed after notation minted
acceptance_tests: facets are mutually exclusive on a test sample

nodes.definition: Design notation, codes, or URIs that name and order concepts and support hospitality for growth.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when notation runs out of room to insert new concepts

pros.claim: stable identifiers enable citation, linking, and persistent references
pros.example: persistent URIs let external datasets cite concepts safely

cons.claim: notation/URI changes are highly irreversible and break references
cons.example: renaming a URI invalidates every external link to it

failure_modes: notation lacks hospitality for new topics
URIs reused or recycled across concepts
acceptance_tests: notation supports insertion without renumbering on test cases
URIs are unique and never reused

nodes.definition: Represent the KOS in SKOS: concepts, prefLabel/altLabel, broader/narrower/related, concept schemes, and collections.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when SKOS integrity constraints fail or a new label type is needed

pros.claim: standard model enables interoperable publication and tooling
pros.example: publishing as SKOS lets external apps consume broader/narrower out of the box

cons.claim: SKOS underspecifies semantics, tempting misuse of skos:related
cons.example: using skos:related to fake a missing hierarchical link

acceptance_tests: SKOS integrity checks pass (single prefLabel/lang, acyclic broader)
every concept linked to a scheme
revisit_triggers: new label/relation requirement not in SKOS

nodes.definition: Build or apply a controlled subject-heading list with main headings, subdivisions, and reference structure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when heading-subdivision practice diverges from cataloging rules

pros.claim: provides consistent, predictable access points across a collection
pros.example: 'Water -- Pollution -- United States' gives a predictable browse path

cons.claim: heading strings grow complex and inconsistent without strict rules
cons.example: inconsistent subdivision order splits one topic across headings

nodes.definition: Establish authorized forms for names, places, and entities with variant references and disambiguation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when two entities collapse or one entity splits across records

pros.claim: disambiguates same-named entities and unifies variant forms
pros.example: two authors named 'J. Smith' get distinct authorized records

cons.claim: merging/splitting authority records is disruptive and irreversible
cons.example: an erroneous merge attributes one author's works to another

failure_modes: authority record drift from external identifiers
acceptance_tests: each authorized form is unique and qualified
revisit_triggers: new entity shares an authorized form

nodes.definition: Model places as a geospatial KOS with names, types, footprints, and place-hierarchy relations.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when administrative boundaries or place names change over time

pros.claim: links named places to footprints enabling spatial and named retrieval
pros.example: resolving 'Constantinople' to a footprint and to 'Istanbul' over time

cons.claim: place names and boundaries are time-dependent and contested
cons.example: a single place name maps to different boundaries across eras

acceptance_tests: each place has a feature type and at least one name form

nodes.definition: Manage domain terminology: definitions, term-concept entries, usage status, and term-level metadata.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when domain usage deprecates or introduces terms

pros.claim: definitions and status reduce ambiguity for indexers and users
pros.example: marking a term 'deprecated' steers indexers to its replacement

cons.claim: definition drift across versions confuses long-term users
cons.example: silently changing a definition alters past indexing meaning

acceptance_tests: every preferred term has a definition
status values from a closed set

nodes.definition: Create concept-to-concept mappings/crosswalks (exact/close/broad/narrow/related) between two or more KOS.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when either mapped vocabulary issues a new version

pros.claim: enables cross-system retrieval and data integration across vocabularies
pros.example: mapping a local taxonomy to a national standard lets records be exchanged

cons.claim: wrong mapping relation type silently corrupts integrated retrieval
cons.example: asserting exactMatch where only broadMatch holds over-merges concepts

acceptance_tests: each mapping cites the relation type and evidence
no exactMatch where labels diverge in scope

nodes.definition: Apply lexical, structural, and semantic matching (manual, computational, hybrid) to propose candidate mappings.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when matcher precision/recall drifts below threshold on a gold sample

pros.claim: scales candidate generation across large vocabularies
pros.example: automated matchers propose thousands of candidates for human review

cons.claim: automated matches need adjudication; unreviewed matches inject errors
cons.example: accepting all high-score matches imports false equivalences

failure_modes: matcher tuned to a non-representative sample
acceptance_tests: candidate matches scored and queued for adjudication
revisit_triggers: matcher precision/recall drops on gold sample
vocabulary size grows beyond manual review

nodes.definition: Establish editorial governance, change control, and versioning for the KOS over its lifecycle.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when uncontrolled edits or version ambiguity are detected

pros.claim: prevents uncontrolled drift and supports reproducible references
pros.example: versioned releases let consumers pin to a stable vocabulary state

cons.claim: weak governance makes concept changes silently break downstream data
cons.example: deleting a concept without deprecation breaks every record using it

acceptance_tests: every release has a version and change log

nodes.definition: Evaluate KOS quality: structural integrity, warrant coverage, consistency, and fitness for user tasks.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a release candidate or major structural change is proposed

pros.claim: catches integrity and coverage defects before release
pros.example: cycle detection finds a broader/narrower loop pre-publication

cons.claim: task-fitness is hard to measure without user evaluation data
cons.example: structural checks pass but users still cannot find concepts

failure_modes: only structural checks run, ignoring task fitness

nodes.definition: Evaluate and select an existing KOS to adopt/reuse instead of building, against scope, quality, and licensing.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a higher-quality or better-licensed external KOS becomes available

pros.claim: reuse cuts cost and improves interoperability with adopters
pros.example: adopting a widely-used standard yields ready-made mappings and tooling

cons.claim: adopted KOS may misfit scope and force awkward extensions
cons.example: a generic scheme lacks the domain depth requiring heavy local extension

failure_modes: custom build chosen despite a good fit available
acceptance_tests: candidate KOS scored against scope and quality

edges.why_related: scope and required KOS-type class constrain which structure family can be selected
edges.benefit_of_coupling: type selection grounded in validated scope
edges.risk_of_conflict: selecting type before scope forces rework
edges.example: scope says browse-only so a thesaurus is over-built
edges.resolution_rule: finalize scope statement before locking KOS type

edges.why_related: scope defines the corpus and user community whose warrant is analyzed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: warrant evidence drawn from the correct domain
edges.risk_of_conflict: analyzing warrant on wrong scope wastes effort
edges.example: warrant gathered from a corpus outside the agreed scope
edges.resolution_rule: fix scope before collecting warrant evidence

edges.why_related: scope defines the criteria against which existing KOS are scored for reuse
edges.risk_of_conflict: reuse decided before scope misjudges fit
edges.example: a generic scheme picked before scope shows it lacks depth
edges.resolution_rule: complete scope before reuse evaluation

edges.why_related: the selected KOS type sets how concepts and labels are modeled
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling before type causes structural redo
edges.example: ontology-level concept model built where a taxonomy was chosen
edges.resolution_rule: lock KOS type before concept modeling

edges.why_related: type and expressivity bound the coordination policy options
edges.risk_of_conflict: setting coordination before type is premature
edges.example: postcoordination assumed before type supports it
edges.resolution_rule: decide type before coordination policy

edges.why_related: the chosen type shapes the governance and lifecycle model needed
edges.risk_of_conflict: governance designed for the wrong artifact wastes effort
edges.example: ontology governance overhead applied to a small term list
edges.resolution_rule: select type before designing governance

edges.why_related: warranted term set is the raw material from which concepts are abstracted
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling concepts before warrant invents unused concepts
edges.example: a concept created with no literary or user warrant
edges.resolution_rule: establish warranted terms before concept modeling

edges.why_related: hierarchical relations are asserted between defined concepts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: relations attach to stable concept identities
edges.risk_of_conflict: relating before concepts exist is invalid
edges.example: BT/NT asserted between undefined terms
edges.resolution_rule: define concepts before hierarchy relations

edges.why_related: associative relations link defined concepts
edges.benefit_of_coupling: RT links rest on real concepts
edges.risk_of_conflict: RT before concepts is meaningless
edges.example: RT asserted between non-existent concepts
edges.resolution_rule: define concepts before associative relations

edges.why_related: equivalence groups labels under a concept's preferred term
edges.risk_of_conflict: synonymy without concepts duplicates entries
edges.example: synonyms managed as free terms not under a concept
edges.resolution_rule: define concepts before equivalence control

edges.why_related: notation/URIs are minted to identify defined concepts
edges.risk_of_conflict: minting IDs before concepts causes reuse/collisions
edges.example: a URI minted then reassigned to a different concept
edges.resolution_rule: define concepts before minting notation

edges.why_related: term entries and definitions attach to modeled concepts
edges.risk_of_conflict: defining terms before concepts confuses term vs concept
edges.example: a definition written for a term with no concept
edges.resolution_rule: model concepts before terminology entries

edges.why_related: coordination policy frames whether facet analysis and citation order are needed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: facet work scoped by coordination stance
edges.risk_of_conflict: faceting before policy may be wasted
edges.example: facets built where postcoordination needs none
edges.resolution_rule: set coordination policy before facet analysis

edges.why_related: coordination policy determines heading-string construction rules
edges.risk_of_conflict: headings built before policy are inconsistent
edges.example: subdivision order set before citation-order policy
edges.resolution_rule: fix coordination policy before heading construction

edges.why_related: settling hierarchy first prevents using RT where BT/NT belongs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: RT reserved for true lateral relations
edges.risk_of_conflict: authoring RT first muddles hierarchy
edges.example: RT added then replaced by a discovered BT/NT
edges.resolution_rule: complete hierarchy pass before associative pass

edges.why_related: preferred-term and USE/UF decisions feed heading authorized forms
edges.risk_of_conflict: headings before equivalence use uncontrolled variants
edges.example: a heading authored on a non-preferred variant
edges.resolution_rule: resolve equivalence before authorizing headings

edges.why_related: equivalence/variant logic underlies authorized-form vs variant-form control
edges.risk_of_conflict: authority before equivalence duplicates effort
edges.example: variant forms managed inconsistently across topical and name vocabularies
edges.resolution_rule: establish equivalence policy before authority records

edges.why_related: place-hierarchy relations reuse hierarchical-relation semantics
edges.risk_of_conflict: place hierarchy before relation semantics drifts
edges.example: place containment modeled as isA instead of part-of
edges.resolution_rule: settle hierarchical-relation semantics before gazetteer hierarchy

edges.why_related: concepts are the skos:Concept resources serialized
edges.risk_of_conflict: serializing before concepts are stable churns the graph
edges.example: SKOS export of half-modeled concepts
edges.resolution_rule: stabilize concept model before serialization

edges.why_related: BT/NT relations become skos:broader/narrower
edges.risk_of_conflict: serializing before hierarchy yields incomplete graph
edges.example: SKOS broader links missing for unmodeled relations
edges.resolution_rule: complete hierarchy before serialization

edges.why_related: preferred/variant labels become prefLabel/altLabel
edges.risk_of_conflict: serializing before labels violates prefLabel rules
edges.example: two prefLabels per language exported
edges.resolution_rule: finalize label control before serialization

edges.why_related: stable SKOS concepts/URIs are the endpoints mappings reference
edges.risk_of_conflict: mapping before serialization references unstable IDs
edges.example: a mapping points at a URI that later changes
edges.resolution_rule: serialize and stabilize URIs before mapping

edges.why_related: the mapping requirement and relation-type vocabulary frame what matchers propose
edges.benefit_of_coupling: alignment scoped to required mapping types
edges.risk_of_conflict: running matchers before mapping policy yields unusable candidates
edges.example: matcher outputs relation types the policy disallows
edges.resolution_rule: define mapping policy before running alignment

edges.why_related: the serialized graph is the artifact evaluated for integrity
edges.benefit_of_coupling: evaluation runs on the canonical artifact
edges.risk_of_conflict: evaluating before serialization tests a draft
edges.example: integrity checks on an unpublished spreadsheet
edges.resolution_rule: serialize before structural evaluation

edges.why_related: warrant set is the baseline for coverage evaluation
edges.risk_of_conflict: evaluating coverage without warrant is arbitrary
edges.example: coverage judged against designer opinion not warrant
edges.resolution_rule: establish warrant before coverage evaluation

edges.why_related: evaluation defects trigger revision of the serialized model
edges.benefit_of_coupling: defects routed back to the model
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded re-evaluation loops stall release
edges.example: each eval cycle finds new minor defects forever
edges.resolution_rule: stop when no failing structural checks remain or max 5 cycles

edges.why_related: coverage gaps trigger adding or splitting concepts
edges.risk_of_conflict: re-modeling loops without stop criteria
edges.example: concepts churned each evaluation pass
edges.resolution_rule: stop when warrant coverage exceeds threshold or max 5 cycles

edges.why_related: versioning and deprecation rules constrain how the serialized graph may change
edges.risk_of_conflict: ungoverned edits break consumers
edges.example: a concept deleted from the graph without deprecation
edges.resolution_rule: governance rules bound serialization changes; deprecate not delete

edges.why_related: version control of source/target vocabularies bounds mapping validity
edges.risk_of_conflict: unversioned mappings silently rot
edges.example: a mapping breaks when target vocabulary changes unversioned
edges.resolution_rule: pin mappings to vocabulary versions under governance

edges.why_related: facet structure and citation order change the notation/ordering design
edges.risk_of_conflict: notation fixed before facets forces rework
edges.example: compound notation cannot encode a new facet order
edges.resolution_rule: design notation to accommodate facet citation order

edges.why_related: an adopted external KOS constrains the local concept model to extension points
edges.risk_of_conflict: reusing then heavily remodeling defeats reuse
edges.example: local model forks the adopted scheme incompatibly
edges.resolution_rule: extend rather than fork the adopted KOS where feasible

edges.why_related: both are controlled-vocabulary application artifacts at the term/heading level
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them merges distinct artifact types
edges.example: treating a heading list as a term base loses subdivision semantics
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct; reuse label-control conventions, not structure

edges.why_related: both manage authorized vs variant forms for named entities
edges.risk_of_conflict: merging them ignores geospatial vs name-specific needs
edges.example: applying person-name rules to places drops footprints
edges.resolution_rule: share entity-control patterns but keep type-specific fields

edges.why_related: both rely on gold-sample scoring against precision/recall thresholds
edges.benefit_of_coupling: reuse of evaluation harness for matcher scoring
edges.risk_of_conflict: conflating them hides that one tests mappings, other tests the KOS
edges.example: matcher precision reported as KOS quality
edges.resolution_rule: share scoring harness; report metrics against the correct target

edges.why_related: precoordination expressivity pressure pushes the type toward enumerative complexity that conflicts with a lean type choice
edges.risk_of_conflict: silent over-coordination inflates the vocabulary
edges.example: forcing precoordinated strings turns a simple taxonomy into a heading syntax
edges.resolution_rule: user-task precision needs dominate; choose minimum coordination that meets retrieval SLO

edges.why_related: mapping stability pressure conflicts with frequent versioning of the mapped vocabularies
edges.risk_of_conflict: unmanaged versioning breaks mappings
edges.example: a new vocabulary version invalidates a published crosswalk
edges.resolution_rule: governance dominates: pin mappings to versions and schedule mapping revalidation per release

edges.why_related: automated-alignment throughput pressure conflicts with evaluation rigor needed before publishing mappings
edges.risk_of_conflict: publishing unadjudicated matches injects errors
edges.example: high-score auto-matches shipped without review
edges.resolution_rule: evaluation/adjudication dominates: no auto-match published below precision threshold

edges.why_related: enumerative deep-hierarchy pressure conflicts with analytico-synthetic faceted decomposition
edges.risk_of_conflict: mixing paradigms yields an inconsistent scheme
edges.example: one branch enumerated, a sibling faceted, confusing users
edges.resolution_rule: pick one dominant paradigm per area; facet where combination is high, enumerate where stable

conflict_axes.trigger: deciding whether to combine subjects at index time or search time
resolution_order: profile user query behavior and system capability
measure precision/recall and false-coordination risk
choose minimum coordination meeting the retrieval SLO
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: user-task precision/recall needs dominate; do not precoordinate beyond what the system cannot postcoordinate
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if neither option meets precision and recall targets simultaneously
conflict_axes.example: enumerating all subject combinations as headings vs leaving them to AND-queries

conflict_axes.trigger: richer KOS type/relations raise authoring and maintenance burden
resolution_order: estimate authoring/maintenance cost per expressivity level
weigh against retrieval/inference payoff
pick the leanest type meeting warranted tasks
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: fitness-for-task dominates: add expressivity only where a user task requires it
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if maintenance capacity cannot sustain the chosen expressivity
conflict_axes.example: an OWL ontology chosen where a SKOS taxonomy would meet every task

conflict_axes.trigger: warrant sources disagree on whether a term/structure is justified
resolution_order: record each warrant type per disputed term
apply the warrant-precedence policy
escalate ties to subject expert
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: user warrant dominates for access points; literary warrant dominates for definitional scope
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if user and literary warrant conflict on a high-frequency term
conflict_axes.example: literary warrant supports a term users never query

conflict_axes.trigger: a broader/narrower link could be read as isA or part-of
resolution_order: classify each BT as generic, instance, or partitive
forbid mixing kinds on one transitive chain
validate subsumption inference on a sample
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: semantic correctness dominates: never assert a BT that breaks transitive isA inference
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a needed navigation requires mixing partitive and generic links

conflict_axes.trigger: treating near-synonyms as equivalent boosts recall but loses precision
resolution_order: test whether the distinction matters for user tasks
prefer separate concepts when a real distinction exists
add scope notes to disambiguate
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: precision dominates when a documented distinction affects retrieval; otherwise favor recall
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if collapsing terms would merge concepts users must distinguish
conflict_axes.example: 'efficacy' vs 'effectiveness' wrongly merged into one term

conflict_axes.trigger: asserting exactMatch widely improves coverage but risks over-merging
resolution_order: require evidence for exactMatch vs broad/close/relatedMatch
default to weaker relation under uncertainty
queue uncertain matches for human adjudication
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: mapping precision dominates: never assert exactMatch where concept scope diverges
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a high-value integration needs exactMatch the evidence cannot support
conflict_axes.example: broadMatch upgraded to exactMatch to simplify a crosswalk

conflict_axes.trigger: an existing KOS is available but does not perfectly fit scope
resolution_order: score candidate fit, quality, governance, and license
estimate extension cost vs build cost
prefer reuse+extension when interoperability value is high
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: interoperability and cost dominate unless the misfit forces incoherent extensions
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if extension to fit would fork the adopted scheme incompatibly
conflict_axes.example: adopting a national scheme that lacks a required domain branch

conflict_axes.trigger: concept evolution pressures URIs/notation that consumers depend on
resolution_order: never reuse or recycle retired identifiers
deprecate concepts instead of deleting
version and document every breaking change
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: identifier stability dominates: persistence guarantees override convenient renumbering
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a needed restructuring cannot preserve external references
conflict_axes.example: renaming a URI breaks every external dataset citing it

conflict_axes.trigger: scaling alignment with automation pressures skipping human adjudication
resolution_order: score candidates against a gold sample
set a precision threshold for auto-accept
route sub-threshold matches to human review
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: human review dominates for published mappings; automation only proposes, never authorizes
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if review backlog blocks a required integration deadline
conflict_axes.example: auto-accepting all high-score matches imports false equivalences

edge_cases.trigger: a broader/narrower chain forms a loop
edge_cases.detection_method: run transitive closure / cycle detection over skos:broader

edge_cases.trigger: two prefLabels in the same language on one concept
edge_cases.detection_method: validate one prefLabel per language per concept

edge_cases.trigger: a synonym modeled as a separate concept
edge_cases.detection_method: cluster labels by definition and detect near-duplicate concepts
resolution: merge into one concept with alt labels

edge_cases.trigger: generic and partitive links share a transitive chain
edge_cases.detection_method: type-check each BT link kind along inference chains

edge_cases.failure_mode: false drops or false hits in retrieval
edge_cases.example: false drops or false hits in retrieval
edge_cases.detection_method: audit sample queries for false-coordination errors
resolution: add precoordinated strings for risky combinations

edge_cases.detection_method: spot-check mappings: compare scope notes of mapped concepts
check that every published mapping has an adjudication status

edge_cases.trigger: a retired identifier reassigned to a new concept
edge_cases.failure_mode: external references resolve to the wrong concept
edge_cases.example: external references resolve to the wrong concept
edge_cases.detection_method: diff identifier registry across versions for reuse of retired IDs
resolution: deprecate the old concept with a note

edge_cases.trigger: a concept deleted instead of deprecated
edge_cases.failure_mode: downstream records reference a missing concept
edge_cases.example: downstream records reference a missing concept
edge_cases.detection_method: check change log: deletions without deprecation entries

edge_cases.failure_mode: release stalls under endless minor revisions
edge_cases.example: release stalls under endless minor revisions
edge_cases.detection_method: track defect-count delta per cycle against materiality threshold
resolution: apply stop condition (no failing structural checks or max 5 cycles)

edge_cases.trigger: mapped vocabulary issues a new version
edge_cases.detection_method: compare mapping target versions against latest released versions

edge_cases.trigger: historic and current place names/boundaries conflated
edge_cases.detection_method: check place records for temporal coverage on names and footprints

workflow.objective: fix domain scope, user tasks, warrant sources, and build-vs-reuse decision
entry_criteria: sample corpus and query logs available
acceptance_tests: scope statement names tasks and warrant types

handoff_artifact.required_contents: scope statement; KOS-type requirement; reuse decision; warrant sources

workflow.do_first_because: scope is the highest-coupling foundation every later step depends on

workflow.objective: select KOS type, coordination policy, and governance/versioning model

handoff_artifact.required_contents: selected type; coordination policy; governance scheme; rationale

workflow.do_first_because: type and coordination decisions bound all modeling and irreversibly shape notation

workflow.objective: gather literary, user, and structural warrant for candidate terms
acceptance_tests: each included term cites a warrant source

handoff_artifact.required_contents: warranted terms; warrant evidence; exclusion list

workflow.do_first_because: warrant grounds concept modeling and is needed before authoring concepts

workflow.objective: model concepts, preferred/variant labels, and definitions
acceptance_tests: one preferred label per language per concept

handoff_artifact.required_contents: concept inventory; labels; synonym rings; definitions

workflow.do_first_because: concepts are the units all relations, notation, and serialization attach to

workflow.objective: assert hierarchical then associative relations with correct semantics

handoff_artifact.required_contents: BT/NT set; RT set; relation-kind decisions

workflow.do_first_because: hierarchy first prevents misusing RT and keeps inference valid

workflow.objective: design notation/URIs, facets/citation order, headings, authority and place records

handoff_artifact.required_contents: notation/URI policy; facet scheme; heading rules; authority/place records

workflow.do_first_because: notation/URIs are highly irreversible and must be designed before publication

workflow.objective: serialize the KOS in SKOS with concepts, labels, relations, schemes, collections
entry_criteria: concept model, relations, labels, and notation soft-locked
workflow.do_first_because: the canonical SKOS artifact is what evaluation and mapping operate on

workflow.objective: create and adjudicate mappings/crosswalks to other vocabularies
acceptance_tests: each mapping cites relation type and evidence

handoff_artifact.required_contents: mapping set; crosswalk; relation justifications; adjudication log

workflow.do_first_because: mappings require stable URIs and must be adjudicated before publication

workflow.objective: evaluate structural integrity, warrant coverage, consistency, and task fitness
workflow.do_first_because: evaluation must pass before any hard lock or release

workflow.objective: apply change control, version, and release under governance
entry_criteria: human review of high-risk nodes complete
acceptance_tests: release has version and change log

handoff_artifact.required_contents: versioned release; change log; deprecation register; approvals

workflow.do_first_because: hard lock only after dependency, validation, and human-review gates pass

dominance_rules.trigger: a change speeds delivery but risks correctness or interoperability
dominance_rules.rule: never accept a delivery shortcut that fails integrity or mapping correctness
dominance_rules.example: skip evaluation to ship faster rejected after cycle was found

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node is unblocked but its prerequisites are unmet
dominance_rules.rule: do not finalize a node before its declared prerequisites are reviewed
dominance_rules.example: mapping authored before SKOS URIs stabilized rejected

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric estimate looks precise but lacks an eligible source
dominance_rules.rule: label values heuristic unless an eligible source supports a stronger label
dominance_rules.required_action: downgrade any observed/experimental label without data
dominance_rules.example: a confidence value labeled observed with no dataset downgraded

dominance_rules.trigger: a release is pressured to lock before evaluation completes
dominance_rules.rule: no hard lock before structural integrity and coverage checks pass
dominance_rules.required_action: hold lock until KOS_EVALUATION and human review pass
dominance_rules.example: hard-locking a vocabulary with an undetected broader cycle blocked

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk decision is proposed for automation
dominance_rules.rule: irreversible/high-risk decisions require human review and a decision record
dominance_rules.example: auto-merging two authority records requires human sign-off

dominance_rules.rule: never reuse or recycle retired identifiers; deprecate, do not delete
dominance_rules.required_action: mint new URIs and deprecate old ones
dominance_rules.example: renaming a URI to clean up notation blocked

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient navigation link would violate relation semantics
dominance_rules.rule: do not assert a BT/NT that breaks transitive isA inference
dominance_rules.required_action: use skos:related or a partitive relation instead
dominance_rules.example: placing a part under a generic parent for browse convenience blocked

dominance_rules.trigger: a mapping/metric is asserted without supporting evidence
dominance_rules.rule: every non-heuristic claim and every exactMatch must cite evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: attach evidence or downgrade the assertion
dominance_rules.example: exactMatch without scope comparison downgraded to closeMatch

dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to add many concepts threatens schema/identity stability
dominance_rules.rule: schema and concept-identity rules dominate over raw concept count
dominance_rules.required_action: freeze identity rules before bulk authoring
dominance_rules.example: bulk-importing terms before identity policy rejected

dominance_rules.trigger: objects are created without traceable warrant or source
dominance_rules.rule: no node/edge/mapping without warrant or source reference
dominance_rules.example: a concept with no warrant or source removed

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient hierarchy edge would create a cycle
dominance_rules.rule: dependency and broader/narrower graphs must remain acyclic
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker link to related or sequence
dominance_rules.example: a broader cycle resolved by demoting one link to related

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve scope and user tasks before selecting KOS type
anti_rework_rules.rationale: type chosen on wrong scope forces full restructuring
anti_rework_rules.example: an ontology chosen then dropped after scope showed browse-only need

anti_rework_rules.rationale: concepts without warrant get pruned later
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: concepts authored with no warrant evidence
anti_rework_rules.example: a concept created then removed for lacking warrant

anti_rework_rules.rationale: relations between undefined concepts are invalid and re-done
anti_rework_rules.example: relations re-authored after concepts were renamed

anti_rework_rules.rationale: RT added prematurely is replaced once hierarchy is settled
anti_rework_rules.example: an RT later found to be a BT/NT and redone

anti_rework_rules.rule: set coordination policy before building headings/facets
anti_rework_rules.rationale: headings/facets built on wrong coordination need rework
anti_rework_rules.example: subdivision order redone after citation-order policy set

anti_rework_rules.rationale: URI churn after serialization breaks references
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: serialization run before URI policy frozen

anti_rework_rules.rationale: mappings on unstable URIs break when URIs change
anti_rework_rules.example: a crosswalk pointing at a since-changed URI

anti_rework_rules.rule: run evaluation and human review before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking before evaluation embeds defects irreversibly
anti_rework_rules.example: a vocabulary hard-locked with an undetected cycle

anti_rework_rules.rule: adjudicate automated matches before publishing mappings
anti_rework_rules.rationale: publishing unreviewed matches injects errors at scale
anti_rework_rules.example: false mappings shipped from unadjudicated candidates

anti_rework_rules.rationale: deletion breaks downstream records that re-key later
anti_rework_rules.example: records pointing at a deleted concept break

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete traceability matrix before hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: untraceable objects cannot be impact-analyzed on change
anti_rework_rules.example: a mapping with no source ref blocks impact analysis

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or evaluation reports a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report and evaluation deltas to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk_score and irreversibility
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue ordered and no high-risk defect unranked

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect or change affects a soft/hard-locked or high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependencies and mappings downstream of the change
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact closed for the change set

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is assigned for repair
a repair touches a locked or high-coupling component
new evidence or evaluation shifts a node's importance
iteration_protocol.detection: compare posterior delta to posterior_revisit_delta threshold
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: posterior delta below 0.10 for all nodes

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream change invalidates a downstream lock
iteration_protocol.detection: detect changes to nodes a locked node depends on
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no locked node has an unreviewed upstream change

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is high-risk, irreversible, or low-confidence
iteration_protocol.detection: check risk_if_wrong>=0.80 or confidence below review threshold

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new release candidate is prepared
iteration_protocol.detection: compare metrics against the previous version
action: diff structural and coverage metrics vs prior version
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: regression report shows no material regression

iteration_protocol.trigger: low-risk defects remain but gates pass
iteration_protocol.detection: count residual low-risk defects against tolerance
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: residual low-risk defects within tolerance and gates pass

human_review_required_for: KOS type selection for irreversible adoption

checks.repair_action: converted two eval feedback links to feedback edges with stop conditions
recomputed all derived fields from formulas

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked structural change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when a warrant or evidence label is revised
downgrade mappings when a mapped vocabulary version changes
